title: Meal Combo Builder
statement: A restaurant menu has 12 side dishes. The ordering screen must list every possible set of sides a customer could pick (including none), so staff can price them.
constraints: n = 12, every set must be listed

approaches.name: Backtracking over take or skip for each side
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: The output itself has 2¹² = 4,096 sets, so listing them is the minimum work.

approaches.name: Count from 0 to 2ⁿ − 1 and read each number's bits as take or skip
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Same cost; a good alternative when n is at most about 20.

approaches.name: Write one nested loop per side
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: Correct for exactly 12 sides, but breaks as soon as the menu changes.

approaches.name: Add sides one by one, keeping only the cheapest set
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: Gives one set, not every set.

title: Seating Plan Search
statement: A wedding planner must seat 10 guests in a row of 10 chairs so that no two guests who dislike each other sit next to each other. Only one valid seating is needed, and there are 15 "dislike" pairs.
examples: Find any order of the 10 guests with no dislike pair adjacent

approaches.name: Backtracking that places guests chair by chair and abandons a branch as soon as two neighbours dislike each other
approaches.label: best
approaches.time: O(n!) worst case, far less in practice
approaches.why: Bad partial seatings are cut off before they grow, and the search stops at the first valid seating.

approaches.name: Generate all 3,628,800 orders, then check each one
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Correct but checks every full order, even ones that failed at the second chair.

approaches.name: Shuffle the guests until a valid order appears
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: May never finish, and cannot tell when no seating exists.

title: Word in a Letter Grid
statement: A puzzle app checks whether a word of up to 12 letters can be traced in a 6 × 6 letter grid by moving up, down, left or right, without reusing a cell.
examples: grid with A B C / S F C / A D E, word ABCCED → true

approaches.name: From each cell matching the first letter, DFS letter by letter, marking cells in use and unmarking when backing up
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: Mismatched letters prune almost every branch at once.

approaches.name: List every path of length L in the grid, then compare with the word
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Correct, but builds paths that fail at their first letter.

approaches.name: Check that the grid contains every letter of the word
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: Necessary but not enough: the letters must also be adjacent in order.

approaches.name: BFS from the first letter without tracking used cells
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: Cannot tell which cells a particular path has already used.
